notes: Dawenkou culture of Shandong; the page says 'The culture existed from 4300 to 2600 BC' (infobox 'c. 4300 - c. 2600 BC') and divides it into 'the early phase (4100-3500 BC), the middle phase (3500-3000 BC) and the late phase (3000-2600 BC)'; the Beixin page says '(4100-2600 BC)'. The dossier starts at 4100, the Beixin hand-over and the early phase's start; the extra two centuries of the infobox are not drawn (disagreement). Extent: 'primarily located in the eastern province of Shandong', also 'in Anhui, Henan and Jiangsu'; no area, no site count. Shandong plus the Beixin discs (which reach northern Jiangsu) are drawn; the page says rice was more important at the southern sites. The page's Liangzhu and Majiabang remarks are influence ('The Majiabang ... northern Jiangsu sites were of the Dawenkou culture' is on the Majiabang page), so the border with the Majiabang is the Yangtze-side edge of the Xuzhou disc, a placement. Yangshao: the page speaks of 'a dynamic interchange' with the Yangshao 'over two and a half millennia'; the Henan border is not on either page. The end: Longshan followed, 'Shandong Longshan ... inherited much of its ancestry from Dawenkou' and its 'early variant corresponds to the latest Dawenkou layer'; no dossier for the Longshan yet (counterpart). One sentence of the page dates the Jiahu link '(2600 BC+-4300 BC)', an obvious page error not used. No Cliopatria shape, no area figure.
